#5133. Can Institutions Secretly Buy Billions of XRP? Ripple Veteran Says It Is 'Not Impossible'

Ripple’s longtime CTO emeritus David Schwartz does not think institutions can privately snap up billions of XRP via dark pools without affecting the token’s price on public markets.

"I don't think so. Who are they buying the XRP from? Why wouldn't people generally want the price to rise when they buy? But it's not impossible," Schwartz wrote on X on Nov. 24.

This was in response to a question posed by an XRP community member wondering if private trading platforms might give institutions an advantage over retail investors.

Earlier in the conversation, Schwartz noted the pros and cons of dark pools for retail traders.

He mentioned one disadvantage: less efficient price discovery. Given that bids and offers are obscured, retail traders in public markets have less insight into other traders’ bids and ask prices.

If there is a large XRP holder who is already inclined to sell at the current price, an institution could arrange a private trade with this holder without needing to place a massive buy order on an exchange. They could execute the trade without driving the public price up as they buy.

However, will there be enough sellers interested in offloading billions of XRP like this? One might run out of sellers willing to sell at that price. So, the buyer might need to up the ante to find the next willing seller.

A dark pool can hide order size, but one still needs someone on the other side to execute that order.

Plus, a buyer will naturally prefer not to tip its hand while accumulating a position.

Schwartz left open the possibility of a private purchase at scale, but the possibility is rather low.

When asked why XRP Ledger developments were not doing anything for XRP’s price on Nov. 9, Schwartz pointed to the broader crypto market.

He also debunked the notion that Ripple had some secret plan it was not sharing with holders. The company regularly talks about its plans.

Schwartz also mentioned a practical benefit of XRP being worth more in the: a higher price could mean cheaper liquidity provision and less slippage (the difference between the expected price a trader pays and the price they actually pay).

At the same time, he was less convinced that demand for XRP to pay transaction fees could have a big impact on the price by itself.

#5131. Ethereum Foundation Sounds Alarm Over AI Threats

The Ethereum Foundation has been working for years to secure the network against a future in which quantum computing breaks the cryptography underpinning Ethereum, but it is now facing a new and more immediate concern around artificial intelligence.

AI is identifying bugs in live software more quickly than human reviewers can keep up with, and the Ethereum Foundation has now doubled the size of its protocol security team, according to a recent announcement.

As Kev Wedderburn wrote in a post from Devcon, AI models are now identifying thousands of bugs in the Linux kernel, one of the most scrutinized codebases in the world.

For Ethereum developers, the immediate challenge is ensuring that bugs are not present in their software before an upgrade.

The longer-term challenge is mathematical. Ethereum uses digital signatures to identify who can spend funds and which validators have approved the state of the chain.

Wedderburn says that AI's advances in analyzing decades-old algorithms raise questions about the mathematical assumptions underlying those signatures that researchers should consider.

It is not clear whether AI could break Ethereum's existing cryptography. However,  the Ethereum Foundation wants work on new cryptography to be underway.

After more than a year of considering various signature schemes, the Ethereum Foundation has decided to replace elliptic-curve signatures with hash-based cryptography.

The argument is that Ethereum already relies on cryptographic hash security, and by using hashes for signatures too, it can remove an additional assumption about the difficulty of solving mathematical problems associated with elliptic curves.

The proposal affects three areas of Ethereum.

It would see validators use hash-based keys for their signatures, which in turn changes how block finality is determined on the network.

Wallet developers would need to provide users with a way to transition their accounts to hash-based signatures.

And Ethereum's change to the cryptography used for commitments to data (blobs) that rollups publish to the network would require adjustments from rollups too.

One challenge is the size of the signatures. Hash-based signatures are much larger, so developers need to consider how that affects the hardware needed to run a node at home.

Staking pools and multisig wallets would need adjustments too. So would smart contracts that rely on existing cryptography.

There will also be a need to adjust tools that rely on the signature scheme currently used by Ethereum validators (BLS).

#5127. Bitcoin Crash Leaves Strategy $12B and Bitmine $10B Underwater: How Much Worse Can It Get?

Strategy MSTR stock hit a two-year low and trades below its bitcoin. We modeled MSTR and Bitmine if Bitcoin loses $55,000.

Strategy MSTR stock closed at $77.80 on Friday, November 20, its lowest close in at least two years, after a crypto sell-off sent Bitcoin (BTC) toward $55,000. Tom Lee’s Bitmine Immersion (BMNR) fell 14% the same day to $12.98.

Both stocks have fallen harder than the coins they hold. Since October 6, Strategy MSTR stock has lost 53% while Bitcoin fell 31% to Friday’s close. Bitmine dropped 51% as Ether (ETH) fell 40%.

The two companies are now sitting on big paper losses. Strategy is about $12 billion underwater on its Bitcoin, and Bitmine roughly $10 billion on its Ethereum.

The dots aren’t done. pic.twitter.com/y92ITprFKE

— Michael Saylor (@saylor) November 22, 2026

Both stocks bounced about 8% to 9% in pre-market trading on Monday. Yet the recovery remains uncertain, as Bitcoin still needs a daily close above $62K to confirm the reversal. So, how deep is the hole, and what happens to MSTR and BMNR if BTC loses $55,000?

Strategy owned 850,849 BTC as of November 15, bought for $64.20 billion at an average of $75,452 per coin, its latest SEC filing shows.

With Bitcoin at $61,345, that stack is worth about $52.2 billion. That leaves Strategy 19% below its cost, a paper loss of around $12 billion. Bitcoin needs to climb about 23% just to get the company back to break-even.

The bigger problem for shareholders is the valuation. Counting its debt and preferred stock, and netting out cash, the company is valued at about 0.94 times its bitcoin, our estimate shows. Strategy MSTR stock used to trade at a premium to its coins, and that premium paid for the buying.

Below one, the model works in reverse. Selling new shares to buy bitcoin shrinks each share’s claim on the coins. Strategy kept doing it anyway, selling 2.1 million MSTR shares in the week to November 15 to buy 485 BTC at $68,887. It also spent $228 million buying back its STRC preferred stock.

The debt is not the immediate threat. Strategy owes about $6.7 billion in convertible notes and has $14.1 billion of preferred stock, roughly $20.8 billion in all. Its bitcoin would only fall below that if BTC dropped to about $24,500, and it holds a $4.75 billion cash reserve to pay dividends.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Reveals Upcoming Binance Listings

Bitmine held 6,077,745 ETH as of November 15, about 5% of all Ether, the company said in its weekly update. It bought another 7,653 ETH that week.

Bitmine does not publish an average cost. On-chain analysts put it at about $3,353 per ETH, which means the stack cost roughly $20.4 billion. At $1,724, it is worth $10.5 billion. That is a paper loss of about $9.9 billion, or 49%.

“ETH tumbled 28% in the past two weeks,” Lee said in the update. He tied the drop to selling around Nvidia and the run-up to Anthropic’s listing.

BMNR stock trades at about 0.73 times the value of its crypto, cash and stakes. Bitmine carries no debt, only $350 million of preferred stock, so it faces no forced selling. But like Strategy, it can no longer raise money by selling shares without costing existing holders.

EXPLORE: BitMine’s Estimated $3.6B ETH Loss Overshadows Stock Edge

To see what another leg down would do, we ran both treasuries across Bitcoin prices from $40,000 to $80,000. ETH tends to fall harder than Bitcoin. Over the past year, it moved about 1.25 times as much as BTC on a typical day, so we scaled ETH by that.

A drop to $49,000, the August 2024 crash low, would take Strategy’s loss to $22.5 billion, 35% below cost. Bitmine would be down about 61%.

The stocks would likely fall further than that. Since October 6, Strategy MSTR stock has moved about 1.7 times as much as Bitcoin, and BMNR about 1.3 times as much as Ether. Neither company has to sell coins, but a longer stretch below their holdings would shut off the share sales that funded their buying.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Top Solana Meme Coins to Bid

BTC trades at $61,345, below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $73,000, and its 200-day EMA at $75,000.

For Strategy and Bitmine, $55,130 is the number that matters. A daily close below it would push Strategy’s paper loss past $17 billion and put Bitmine down more than half.

JPMorgan is convinced that we are still in the thick of an  “AI supercycle”, with Michael Burry seeming to concur with this theory as his stock portfolio turned highly bullish.

In a recent client research note, JPMorgan’s Head of Global Markets Strategy Dubravko Lakos-Bujas wrote that the AI supercycle is still continuing despite the recent downturn.

“We remain of the view that the AI supercycle remains intact with demand for compute still strong and sticky.”

The note proceeded to set a year-end 2027 target for the S&P 500 at 8,200, implying a 13.9% upside from the 7,201 previous close. While positive, the projection is more conservative than that of Wall Street peers Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs, which both forecast a surge to 8,700.

Even more, the investment company predicts that the S&P 500 earnings per share (EPS) will reach $430 in 2027. This would represent a 15%-17% growth rate from the full year 2026 operating EPS estimate of $368-$374, and a moderation from this year’s 35% estimated growth rate.

JPMorgan highlighted Nvidia and Micron among its favored stocks, in addition to energy infrastructure providers like GE Vernova and Constellation Energy. CoinPedia has covered the 12-month projections for both Nvidia and Micron, which are largely optimistic and bullish.

The bank noted two prevailing headwinds for the S&P 500 performance, including slowed growth in traditional software and the possibility of Fed interest rate hikes as the year draws to an end.

Meanwhile, Michael Burry – the investor famous for prediction and profiting from the 2008 market crash – is now bullish on stocks.

In a recent blog, Burry said he is mostly long on stocks now, with the exception of Palantir and MetLife. Seven of the companies he is long on are part of the S&P 500, including Adobe and PayPal.

His move is meant to lock in profits from the recent tech sell-off, with the intention of profiting from Nvidia stock when optimism is high at the $200 mark. For now, he says the market has priced in any downside especially following CEO Jensen Huang’s return.

In September 2025, attackers exploited the Shibarium bridge and withdrew about $2.4 million worth of assets from it.

According to Shibariumscan, Shibarium processed 546 transactions in a single day in late November, and on Oct. 31, the daily number of transactions on the network was 6,370. Since its launch in August 2023, Shibarium has processed more than 1.5 billion transactions in total.

At the same time, the number of SHIB holders on Ethereum passed 1.7 million on Nov. 17, according to Etherscan.

Attackers have intercepted the Bitcoin mining process, allowing them to divert up to 1.9EH/s of compute to mine rewards for their wallets.

Bitcoin mining company Braiins urged prompt migration to Stratum V2 and TLS or upgrading mining software to versions that perform identity verification before handing off mining pools.

Rumours of OpenAI and Anthropic breaking cryptographic security models continue to swirl, with employees reportedly calling for a pause in AI training citing takeover fears.

More than 1,600 Bitcoin (BTC) mining sites have been hit by a Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) attack, also known as a man-in-the-middle hijack, where attackers impersonate a miner to steal their BTC mining proceeds.

According to Bitcoin mining company Braiins, the attack began in early November, with attackers diverting around 175 petahashes per second (PH/s) of compute from miners in Brazil and Argentina. On November 20, the event spread to Europe, hitting more than 1,000 mining sites in a single second. This time the stolen hashrate grew tenfold to 0.6-1.9 exahashes/second (EH/s).

Notably, Stratum V1 is a protocol that coordinates communication between Bitcoin mining rigs (ASICs) and mining pools. There has, however, been a campaign to push miner migration to Stratum V2 due to the vulnerabilities inherent to the former.

Stratum V1 is unencrypted, has zero server authentication, and is centralized. These features make it prone to internet traffic interception, with attackers impersonating BTC mining pools to feed miners real work while reaping the proceeds to their wallets.

In 2014, Dell’s cybersecurity branch, SecureWorks, uncovered a similar incident. However, by this time, attackers had managed to make away with $83,000 of BTC and other proof-of-work mining rewards.

Braiins urges operators to immediately abandon unencrypted connections, moving instead to Stratum V2, which is decentralized and performs server authentication. The company also released an updated software to block plain-text fallbacks. Even more, Braiins launched a free local SV2 Proxy tool so that older mining rigs can benefit from encrypted processes even though they are incompatible with Stratum V2 and TLS (Transport Layer Security).

Furthermore, the company has asked other mining software providers to update their product to versions that support identity verification. Meanwhile, hosted miners should ask their operators to confirm the security of their main and backup connections.

Recently trending is the rumour that OpenAI and Anthropic AI models may have successfully broken modern cryptographic models. These include Bitcoin’s elliptic curve cryptography (ECC), integer factorization in P, and Ring-LWE.

A Break in ECC would allow private key derivation from public keys, while that in Ring-LWE would make post-quantum migration pointless. Meanwhile, integer factoring in P would affect the majority of the world’s digital infrastructure, including banking systems, government communications, digital authentication, and software signing.

While the allegations remain unconfirmed by said companies, Computer Scientist Scott Aaronson and Ledger CTO Charles Guillemet have mentioned them.

I'm hearing several rumors that frontier labs have broken some major cryptographic primitives:– "Factoring is in P": Now that the Riemann hypothesis is proven, we do understand much better how primes are distributed. Still, I don't think factoring is in P. AKS showed in 2002…

Employees at both companies are also calling for a pause in AI model training, fearing they are capable of causing global chaos through cyberattacks and outages, per Axios.

“If we continue trying to make models much smarter, such that they’re actually smarter than us … they will in fact be able to trick us successfully.”

#5123. Flop Labs Pushes Back Testnet Launch Amid Final Preparations

Flop Labs has announced a minor delay to the launch of its public testnet, pushing back from its previous goal of 15:00 (UTC+8) on November 24.

It's unclear what the reason for the delay is, although the team does expect to launch the testnet before 18:00 (UTC+8) the same day.

Possible reasons for the delay could include conducting final checks, calibrating nodes, validator onboarding, load testing, etc. (although Flop Labs has not confirmed any of these to be the reason for the delay).

It does not appear that Flop Labs has any plans to move the testnet launch to another day.

Flop Labs is building FLOP Network, a blockchain serving as a settlement layer for what it calls the "agentic economy". This would enable AI agents to make payments for computation (e.g. model inference) and memory services, and provide rewards to GPU miners that contribute their computational power to fulfill these requests.

Computation is verified via Flop Labs' "Proof of Useful Inference", which entails miners providing evidence that they've carried out the desired AI computation, and validators checking this evidence.

Why does this matter? FLOP Network would enable agents to make payments for computation, memory, etc. Flop Labs' main competitors include Akash Network and io.net (both of which facilitate access to compute/gpu resources in a decentralized manner), as well as Render Network (which started out facilitating decentralized graphics rendering but has since expanded into AI/compute more broadly).

While Flop Labs' competitors also facilitate access to compute, Flop Labs' main differentiating factor appears to be its focus on facilitating agent-to-agent commerce and computation-verification.

Flop Labs is led by Arthur Hayes, co-founder of crypto exchange BitMEX and current chief investment officer at Maelstrom. The rest of Flop Labs' team includes Sergey Vidyuk (ex-Deutsche Bank/BitMEX) as CTO, and Shu Duan (with experience in investment banking and crypto asset management) as chief strategy officer.

The testnet would be an opportunity to see if Flop Labs can successfully build out its envisioned agentic economy.

#5121. BlackRock ETF Dumps 1 Million ETH Worth $1.75B as Ethereum Outflows Accelerate: Is ETH In Trouble?

BlackRock’s Ethereum ETF has lost over 1 million ETH worth $1.75 billion since October as outflows accelerate.

The BlackRock ETF has shed more than 1 million ETH since October 1, recording net outflows of 1,018,839 ETH worth approximately $1.75 billion. The selling continued on Monday, as BlackRock’s iShares Ethereum Trust (ETHA) transferred another batch of coins to Coinbase Prime.

Between 11:52 and 12:02 UTC, four separate transfers moved 42,631 ETH from BlackRock’s deposit addresses to Coinbase Prime, the brokerage desk handling the fund’s trades. The transfers were worth approximately $73 million at Monday’s prices.

Since October 1, #BlackRock has seen net outflows of 1,018,839 $ETH ($1.75B).https://t.co/YfaFJXVOID pic.twitter.com/tfljcmoSsM

— Lookonchain (@lookonchain) November 23, 2026

The outflows have taken a large bite out of the fund. Comparing Lookonchain’s data with BlackRock’s own filings confirms the match to the coin. ETHA now holds less Ethereum than it did at the end of June.

How much has the BlackRock ETF lost so far, and what might this mean for ETH?

ETHA held 3,675,697 ETH on September 30, its quarterly report shows. On November 20, the iShares fund page listed 2,656,857 ETH.

That is a drop of 1,018,840 ETH, or 28%, which lines up with Lookonchain’s count almost exactly. Shares outstanding fell by a similar amount, from 162.4 million to 119.1 million, as investors cashed out.

The timing stings. In the third quarter, the BlackRock ETF bought 1.19 million ETH for $2.71 billion as money poured back in. Nearly all of that has now left. ETHA’s 2,656,857 ETH is below the 2,695,456 it held on June 30.

The fund’s net assets stood at $4.31 billion on November 20. Its net asset value per share has fallen 41% this year.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best Low-Cap Crypto

We traced the Arkham-labelled addresses in Lookonchain’s screenshot on the Ethereum blockchain. Two BlackRock deposit addresses, 0xC8c5…5b95 and 0x01c2…59E5, sent every transfer to two Coinbase Prime hot wallets.

Since October 1, the two addresses made 84 transfers totalling 1,128,667 ETH. Priced at the hour each one moved, that is about $2.54 billion, or an average of $2,254 per ETH.

The pace picked up in November. The weeks starting November 2 and November 9 each saw more than 200,000 ETH leave, compared with 120,000 to 170,000 a week in October. The biggest single days were October 7, November 10 and November 20, at more than 70,000 ETH each.

The on-chain total is higher than the net drop in holdings because some new money still came in. It also includes Monday’s transfers, which are not yet in the fund’s November 20 figures.

These moves do not mean BlackRock is selling for itself. Coinbase acts as the trust’s agent, and ETHA pays out redemptions either in ETH or in cash raised by selling ETH. When investors leave the fund, the coins go out through Coinbase Prime.

EXPLORE: BitMine’s Estimated $3.6B ETH Loss Overshadows Stock Edge

ETH trades at $1,724, below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $2,131, and its 200-day EMA at $2,248. It fell to $1,538 on November 21, just above its June low of $1,506.

Monday’s 42,631 ETH shows the BlackRock ETF redemptions have not stopped. A pause in transfers to Coinbase Prime would be the first sign the selling is easing.

#5120. Trezor Tells Crypto Users Never to Enter Wallet Backups on Phones Amid Theft Probe

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Crypto wallet provider Trezor has issued a security warning to cryptocurrency users following a recent theft report: "Never type your wallet backup into a phone, app or website."

According to Onchain Lens, a user reported losing over $600,000 across TRON and Solana while using an iPhone 17 Pro Max running iOS 27.2.1. Both the Trezor Safe 7 and the Exodus wallet were reportedly affected. The victim had been using a Trezor Safe 7 for nearly two months.

According to the victim, the Trezor wallet arrived sealed, with no visible tampering; the recovery phrase was generated on the Trezor screen and not on the iPhone; the seed was written on paper and never stored digitally. The victim used Trezor Suite on an iPhone 17 Pro Max via Bluetooth and also had the Exodus wallet on the same iPhone.

The device was running iOS 27.2.1, and the victim never approved the unauthorized transactions. The Trezor wallets for TRON and Solana shared one recovery phrase.

The user said $580,000 was stolen from Trezor on TRON and that an unauthorized transaction moved 49,999 USDT on Nov. 21, 2026. The transaction used the default owner permission, making the signing authority central to the investigation.

Another $23,400 was drained from Trezor on Solana, and the victim says they never approved that transfer using the hardware device. The iPhone remains the main focus, as both Trezor Suite and Exodus were reportedly used on the same iPhone 17 Pro Max running iOS 27.2.1, and both were affected.

Trezor is designed to keep private keys inside the hardware device. However, compromising the phone alone should not normally provide access to Trezor's private keys, and the mechanism behind both thefts remains largely unknown.

On November 9, 2026, Apple issued iOS 27.2.1, which patched several security holes (including some related to Bluetooth). The victim was reportedly running this version when the theft occurred. Thus, there is currently no evidence connecting those vulnerabilities to these transactions. Possible causes outlined included compromised recovery credentials, unauthorized signing, or a device or software security failure.

Trezor responded to this disclosure, saying that Trezor wallets don’t get drained out of nowhere and that there are currently no reports of funds being stolen remotely from any device. It noted that similar cases usually trace back to a compromised wallet backup.

@OnchainLens @binance @Bybit_Official UPDATE: This device came directly from Trezor and shows no sign of an implant. We’re still investigating what happened. So far there’s no confirmed loss of funds from implants and no implant found in any Trezor Safe 7. Never type your wallet backup into a phone, app or website.

In a further update, Trezor confirmed that the device affected came directly from the company and showed no sign of an implant. The wallet provider added that it continues to investigate what happened.

This appears to be a standalone case, as Trezor reiterated that, so far, no confirmed loss of funds from implants has been reported, and no implant has been found in any Trezor Safe 7. It also reiterated an important security warning: users should never enter their wallet backups into a phone, application, or website.

#5117. Another XRP Record Ahead? Ripple CEO Predicts XRP Demand Surge as Inflation-Stricken Markets Seek Alternatives to Fiat

XRP could be on the verge of another major adoption milestone as inflation-hit economies increasingly look for alternatives to traditional currencies. At least that’s according to Brad Garlinghouse.

The Ripple frontman sees growing potential for the cryptocurrency, arguing that demand could rise over time as people in struggling markets seek ways to protect their wealth from weakening fiat currencies. His comments spotlight a potential new driver of XRP adoption and raise fresh questions about how far demand could grow.

Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse believes inflation-hit economies could become an increasingly important source of demand for XRP as people seek alternatives to traditional currencies. Speaking during a recent interview with Bloomberg Television at the Singapore FinTech Festival, he explained how persistent inflation and declining purchasing power could encourage more people to explore digital assets.

“XRP is going to draw people’s interest over time, particularly in markets where you have more inflationary dynamics,” he opined.

Garlinghouse argued that the declining value of fiat currencies could make assets with predictable or limited supplies more attractive to investors. To illustrate his point, he cited the U.S. dollar, describing it as one of the world’s best-managed currencies while noting that it had lost approximately half its value over the past decade.

He added that the situation is considerably worse in countries with weaker monetary management, where some national currencies have reportedly lost between 80% and 90% of their value. Such conditions, in his view, could strengthen the appeal of digital assets whose supplies cannot be expanded at the discretion of central banks or governments.

However, scarcity alone is not enough to attract investors. Garlinghouse also highlighted liquidity as an important consideration, noting that people want assets they can easily hold, transfer, and exchange. This combination could work in XRP’s favor as interest in alternative financial assets grows across inflation-hit markets.

His remarks point to a potential source of XRP demand beyond speculative trading and institutional investment. While increased interest does not guarantee sustained buying pressure or higher prices, broader adoption in economies struggling with currency depreciation could ultimately boost XRP’s long-term appeal.

During the interview, Amin also asked Garlinghouse whether he could see Bitcoin eventually rocketing to the $1 million mark, a target previously floated by several prominent figures in the crypto industry.

The Ripple chief was receptive to the possibility, although he admitted that predicting when such a milestone might happen was difficult. His optimism was largely rooted in the declining purchasing power of traditional currencies rather than any specific Bitcoin price model.

Bitcoin has a hard supply cap of 21 million coins, while XRP’s total supply was established at 100 billion tokens. Their fixed supply structures distinguish them from government-issued currencies, which can be expanded through monetary policy.

Nevertheless, scarcity does not automatically translate into higher valuations or make either cryptocurrency immune to inflation. Both Bitcoin and XRP remain highly volatile assets whose prices are influenced by market demand and broader economic conditions.

Bitcoin surged above $64,400 as it extended its weekend recovery following Friday’s sharp drop below $56,000, while Ripple’s XRP also staged a rebound, briefly reaching $1.02, per CoinGecko. However, both cryptocurrencies have since surrendered part of those gains. At the time of writing, BTC had pulled back to around $61,271, while XRP had also retreated to $0.9435, reflecting renewed selling pressure after the brief recovery.

In periods of competing blocks, Solana validators spend CPU and timing resources replaying blocks that will never make it into the canonical chain once another competing block from the same slot has been finalized.

This PR proposes changes to validator software to help prevent work from being done. It also decouples functionality and gives control to Votor in requesting slot cancellation without modifying BankForks.

Overall, this is a reasonable technical improvement and has a good engineering motivation. Further technical comments and review would be helpful to understand if there are potential race conditions or issues with reliability of replay and consensus. This could be split into two PRs to make it easier to test and review.

Make sure that the replay thread doesn't block on the scheduler finishing processing blocks.

Add slot cancellation, where Votor can tell replay which blocks to stop trying to process.

There was an earlier PR (PR #16454) which attempted to solve a similar problem, but that PR included some complexity around being able to pause and resume block processing.

This PR attempts to solve a similar problem in a simpler way by adding slot cancellation. It allows validators to stop replaying blocks that will never make it into the canonical chain once another block from the same slot has been finalized.

This is an efficiency-focused change to validator software. It's not intended to have a particular effect on transaction throughput or SOL price. For Solana to continue to perform well, it's important not only to continue to increase TPS but also continue to find ways to make sure that validators aren't doing unnecessary work.

For everyday users, it's unlikely there would be noticeable effects from this change. Sending/receiving SOL, using a DEX, using DeFi more broadly, and using any other Solana-powered website/app should all continue to function as normal. It's possible that users could see some benefits from this change in the form of Solana being more performant in the face of heavy compute loads.

Wall Street is closed on Thursday, November 26, for Thanksgiving, with no trading on the New York Stock Exchange or Nasdaq. Stocks return on Friday for a shortened session. Both exchanges will open at the normal time of 9:30 am Eastern, or 8 pm IST, but will shut at 1 pm Eastern, or 11:30 pm IST, three hours ahead of the usual close. That leaves investors with just three and a half hours of trading on Black Friday, compared with six and a half hours on a regular day. Eligible options contracts on the NYSE will stop trading slightly later, at 1:15 pm Eastern, or 11:45 pm IST. The US bond market is also closed on Thursday and will end Friday’s session at 2 pm Eastern. Full trading hours return on Monday, November 30, running from 8 pm to 2:30 am IST. Crypto markets, including Bitcoin and XRP, continue to trade around the clock through the holiday.

#5113. Jensen Huang Recovery Pump Lasted Just Six Hours As BTC Falls Back to $60K – What Went Wrong?

BTC gave back its Nvidia pump in six hours. ETFs keep selling, and Strategy spent $4.30 on STRC per $1 on bitcoin.

Bitcoin was supposed to catch a break. Instead, based on today’s Bitcoin news, November 24, BTC trades near $60,400, below where it stood before Nvidia brought back Jensen Huang. Monday’s excitement barely lasted six hours before the market gave it all back.

Nvidia held on to its gains, closing Monday at $165.05, up 31%. Bitcoin wasn’t so lucky. BTC briefly climbed 5.7% after the announcement, only to slide below its pre-news price by mid-afternoon in New York. By early Tuesday, it had fallen below $61,000 again. Another rally, another disappointment.

The jump that followed Monday’s announcement was gone within six hours.

The selling in this week’s Bitcoin news has company. US spot Bitcoin ETFs posted a fifth straight day of outflows on Monday, and Strategy, the biggest corporate buyer, added just 457 BTC last week.

Strategy has acquired 457 $BTC and repurchased $212M of $STRC. We increased our Digital Credit Securities Repurchase Program by $1B and reallocated $1B from our USD Reserve to USD Cash. As of 11/22/26, we hold 851,305 BTC and $4.8B of USD Assets. $MSTR https://t.co/Wklom6dzrm

— Michael Saylor (@saylor) November 23, 2026

So is Bitcoin’s bounce from $55,000 a real turn, and how much buying is Michael Saylor’s company actually doing?

If you thought you missed yesterday’s reversal and regretted not FOMOing into the pump, you’re probably glad you didn’t. Bitcoin not only gave back the entire pump but also retraced below its initial price before the pump. Absolute cinema.

We tracked Binance’s minute-by-minute BTC price around the Nvidia news.

The contrast with Nvidia is the story. The chipmaker’s rally was about its own leadership, and it held. Bitcoin’s was borrowed, and once traders took profits, nothing was there to keep it up.

That leaves BTC stuck near $60,000, about 10% above Saturday’s two-year low of $55,130 but below the levels it lost last week.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best New Crypto to Hodl

The fund flows behind the Bitcoin news have not turned. US spot Bitcoin ETFs lost a net $569.7 million on Monday, November 23, figures from SoSoValue’s ETF dashboard show. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $509.3 million of it.

It was the fifth straight day of outflows. The week before, the funds lost $1.79 billion, the third-largest weekly outflow since they launched in January 2024. Total net assets have dropped to about $74.1 billion.

That is a lot of selling for one buyer to absorb, even the biggest one.

EXPLORE: Bitcoin Below $62K After Anthropic IPO: Is a SpaceX Style Crash Coming?

Saylor has spent the sell-off signalling that Strategy will keep buying. “The dots aren’t done,” he posted on Sunday, November 22, alongside the company’s purchase tracker.

The filings tell a more cautious story. Strategy bought 457 BTC for $29.6 million in the week to November 22, at an average of $64,898, its latest SEC filing shows. It now holds 851,305 BTC at an average cost of $75,446.

For this Bitcoin news story, we added up Strategy’s three November filings to see where the money went. Strategy raised $705 million by selling MSTR shares over those three weeks. Only $145 million went into bitcoin.

Most of the rest went to buying back STRC, Strategy’s high-yield preferred stock, which has been trading below its face value. Strategy spent $628 million on those repurchases, $4.30 for every $1 it put into bitcoin. Last week, bitcoin took just 12% of the total.

The buying has also slowed fast. Strategy added 1,036 BTC in the first week of November, 485 in the second and 457 in the third. Last week’s $29.6 million equals less than 2% of what the ETFs sold in the week before.

Strategy still has firepower. It raised its buyback limit for preferred stock from $3 billion to $4 billion this week, and it holds $4.8 billion in cash. But MSTR, at $84.40 on Monday, is valued at only about 1.0 times its bitcoin once debt and preferred stock are counted, our estimate shows. At that level, selling new shares no longer adds bitcoin per share, which helps explain why Saylor’s dots keep getting smaller.

BTC trades at $60,448, below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $72,510, and its 200-day EMA at $74,867.

For this Bitcoin news cycle to turn, the ETF selling has to stop first. Until it does, Strategy’s weekly few hundred coins will not be enough to lift BTC above $62,300.

#5109. Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Bill Advances, but Can It Pass Before 2027?

The U.S. House committee advanced a bill that could lock government-held Bitcoin for 20 years.

H.R. 8957 would ban reserve Bitcoin from being sold, swapped or auctioned for two decades.

Following this news, Bitcoin jumped more than 4% after the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve bill advanced.

The House Financial Services Committee has advanced a bill to make the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve, triggering a more than 4% jump in Bitcoin’s price. BTC climbed above $61,000 after falling close to $57,339.

While, hotter than expected U.S. PCE inflation has raised concerns about another Fed rate hike in December.

The House Financial Services Committee has advanced H.R. 8957, the American Reserve Modernization Act of 2026, introduced by Rep. Nicholas J. Begich. The bill aims to establish a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve using Bitcoin seized through criminal and civil asset forfeitures.

The bill passed the committee 28-21 on November 24 and moved to the Union Calendar for a possible House vote. The U.S. government currently holds around 306,800 to 328,000 BTC, mostly seized through asset forfeitures.

Under the bill, the government cannot sell, swap, auction, or use reserve Bitcoin as collateral for at least 20 years. It also rules out borrowing or using new taxes to buy more BTC.

An earlier plan to buy up to one million BTC was removed.

Instead, the Treasury and Commerce departments must study ways to acquire more Bitcoin without using new taxes or debt within 180 days.

The Strategic Bitcoin Reserve currently exists under President Donald Trump’s March 2025 executive order, which a future president could revoke. If passed by both chambers, the bill would establish the reserve under federal law and give it a more permanent legal status.

The bill is now on the Union Calendar, allowing House leaders to schedule a floor vote during the remaining lame-duck session. As of now, no vote date has been announced.

Even if the House approves it in December, the bill must still pass the Senate before Congress ends on January 3, 2027.

The Senate’s crowded year-end schedule, including spending and other must-pass bills, leaves limited time for a standalone crypto bill.

Meanwhile, Polymarket traders see less than a 4% chance of the U.S. making the Bitcoin reserve law before 2027.

Bitcoin price reacted quickly, rising more than 4% and reclaiming $61,000.

The rally came despite hotter U.S. PCE inflation data. November 25 PCE data showed headline inflation rising to 3.8% from 3.6%, while core PCE increased to 3.3% from 3.1%, above the 3.2% forecast.

The higher inflation has pushed expectations of a 25-basis-point Fed rate hike in December to 99%.

On Tuesday morning, the crypto market gave back almost all of the gains it made after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO on Monday. According to CoinMarketCap data, the price of Bitcoin stood at around $60,000 on Tuesday morning, and on Monday evening, Bitcoin was trading as high as $64,372. XRP was back at $0.93 on Tuesday morning after the cryptocurrency reached $1.026 on Monday.

The price of Ethereum was between $1,680 and $1,695 on Tuesday morning, according to CoinMarketCap. In addition, the Crypto Fear and Greed Index stood at 10 on Tuesday, and the index showed extreme fear in the market.

U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs had $569.7 million in net outflows on Monday, Nov. 23, SoSoValue data shows. Spot XRP ETFs in the U.S. also saw outflows on Monday, and the total amount of these outflows was $2.5 million.

On Monday, Nvidia's board voted to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO after input from senior levels of the U.S. government, according to the company's press release. Nvidia shares closed 31.5% higher at $165.05, and the company added $954.3 billion in market value in one session. That is more than twice the previous one-day record of $450 billion that Microsoft set in July.

The S&P 500 gained 4.73% on Monday, and the Nasdaq 100 gained 6.86%. Bitcoin followed the rally and rose to $64,372 on Monday evening, and XRP reached $1.026.

Nvidia shares were down 4.1% at $158.03 in premarket trading on Tuesday, and Nasdaq 100 futures lost 1.62% on Tuesday morning. The VIX rose 8.72% to 28.93 at the same time.

Anthropic shares traded below the $83 IPO price on Tuesday. Earlier, all seven co-founders of the AI company filed to sell a combined $1.96 billion worth of Anthropic stock, or about $280 million each, and there was also news about internal safety problems at Anthropic.

According to CoinGlass data, 146,356 traders were liquidated over the past 24 hours, and the total amount of liquidations reached $875 million.

Short sellers were hit first during Monday's rally, and short positions accounted for $473 million of the total. The largest single liquidation was a $17.83 million BTC-USD position on Hyperliquid. On Tuesday morning, it was the turn of long positions. Over the past 12 hours, longs accounted for $168.85 million out of $207.37 million in liquidations.

Bitcoin dropped as low as $59,366 and was trading at around $60,300 on Tuesday morning, down 1.5% over 24 hours. Bitcoin liquidations amounted to $372.68 million. In addition, open interest in Bitcoin futures rose 1.31% to $39.49 billion as the price was going down.

XRP followed Bitcoin and fell from $1.026 to $0.9238 before it stabilized at around $0.93. XRP liquidations reached $14.05 million over 24 hours, and 3,350 traders were affected. The Coinbase premium for XRP was -0.13%, and the premium for XRP in South Korea was 1.56%.

BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes also commented on the Nvidia rally. According to Hayes, Nvidia's rise is the worst-case scenario for crypto portfolios. Hayes said that crypto needs a crash in U.S. stocks that would force the Fed to start printing money again.

The U.S. Department of Justice has filed a forfeiture complaint against more than $1.1 billion in USDC stablecoins. The funds were stolen from Binance by North Korean hackers on Oct. 29, and Circle helped the authorities with the case. According to the Department of Justice, North Korean hackers stole more than $6 billion from Binance in the attack. Earlier in November, the department said that U.S. authorities and private companies had frozen more than $2.7 billion of the stolen funds.

The Ethereum Foundation also addressed the threat of artificial intelligence. According to the foundation, AI is a more urgent threat to the network than quantum computers. In a blog post, the EF developers said that AI finds vulnerabilities in code faster than auditors can check them, and they also said that AI could break mathematical algorithms that have been used for decades.

EF researcher Justin Drake also spoke about Ethereum's move to hash-based cryptography at Devcon 8 in Mumbai. Drake said that he hoped to complete the transition by December 2028. Earlier, the Ethereum Foundation set December 2029 as the deadline for quantum resistance in its roadmap.

There was other news from regulators and banks as well:

According to Grayscale, the current bear market for Bitcoin has lasted 411 days, and it is the longest one in history. Still, Grayscale called it the mildest one. Bitcoin fell 56% from its October 2025 peak of $124,824 to last week's low of $55,254, according to Grayscale.

Galaxy Research put the drawdown at 53%. According to Galaxy, Bitcoin lost 85%, 84% and 77% in the bear markets of 2013–2015, 2017–2018 and 2021–2022, respectively.

The market capitalization of altcoins excluding Bitcoin and Ethereum dropped to $630.71 billion on Tuesday.

According to CoinGlass data, large buy orders for Bitcoin on OKX and Binance were placed between $59,137 and $59,366 on Tuesday, and $30.3 million worth of long positions could be liquidated in the same range. A large sell order for Bitcoin was placed on Hyperliquid at $60,682, and $64.4 million worth of short positions could be liquidated near $63,996.

The max pain price for Bitcoin options expiring on Nov. 25 stood at $61,000, and the notional value of these options was $642.3 million.

For XRP, liquidations data shows a buy order on Gate at $0.9240 and $577,200 worth of long positions that could be liquidated at $0.9187. Sell orders for XRP on Gate and Hyperliquid were placed between $0.9340 and $0.9444, and $1.4 million worth of short positions could be liquidated at $0.9887.

Two-year U.S. inflation swaps fell to 2.09% ahead of the PCE report, the lowest level for the swaps since September 2024.

#5105. Bitmine Stock: Tom Lee Calls ETH ‘Hard Money’ – But BMNR Share Count Jumps 164%

Tom Lee calls Ethereum hard money as ETH supply growth stays near Bitcoin’s, but Bitmine’s 164% share dilution raises questions for BMNR investors.

Tom Lee made his “hard money” case for Ethereum (ETH) again this Week,  as Bitmine Immersion (BMNR) reported buying another 7,819 ETH last week. Bitmine stock rose 11% the same day, to $14.42, but is still down 44% in a month.

Lee’s argument is about supply. He said ETH’s supply has grown 0.90% a year since Bitmine started buying in June 2025, against 0.82% for Bitcoin (BTC). “In other words, ETH and BTC have essentially the same inflation rate, and both are ‘hard money’ measured in supply growth,” Lee said.

JUST IN: BitMine Immersion buys another 7,819 $ETH, bringing its total holdings to 6,085,564 ETH pic.twitter.com/2LZyEJyyBj

— Coingecko (@coingecko) November 23, 2026

We checked the numbers, and he is right about the coins, but the same test applied to Bitmine’s own shares tells a different story.

Lee’s numbers make a case for ETH as a coin that holds its value. But Bitmine shareholders do not own ETH directly. They own a slice of a company that keeps issuing new shares to buy more of it, and each new share dilutes that slice.

So does the hard-money case for ETH still hold for the people who own Bitmine stock, or is their share of Bitmine’s ETH being watered down faster than ETH’s supply grows?

Lee compared ETH with other big coins in Bitmine’s weekly update. Solana’s supply has grown 7.6% a year over the same period, XRP’s 5.4% and Cardano’s 2.9%, he said. “These others have been far more inflationary.”

Our own check, using CoinGecko’s daily circulating supply over the past 12 months, comes out almost the same:

Ethereum’s supply did grow about as slowly as Bitcoin’s over the past year. Most new ETH paid to validators is offset by the fees the network burns.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Reveals Upcoming Binance Listings

Bitmine paid for its ETH by printing shares. It had 232.4 million shares outstanding on August 31, 2025, and 613.3 million a year later, its annual report shows. By November 4, the count reached 626.5 million.

That is a 164% increase in one fiscal year, about 200 times ETH’s supply growth. Bitmine sold 395 million new shares through its at-the-market program in the Year to August, raising $12.9 billion.

Selling shares to buy ETH works for existing holders when the stock trades above the value of the coins behind it. It hurts when it trades below.

Right now, it trades below. Bitmine says its crypto, cash, and stakes are worth $11.1 billion, about $17.70 per share. At Monday’s close of $14.42, the market values Bitmine stock at roughly 0.81 times its assets, our estimate shows.

Bitmine has pushed back by buying its own shares. It repurchased 20.8 million shares at an average of $17 in July and August, and it has $3.6 billion left under its buyback plan.

EXPLORE: Ethereum News: BitMine To Halt Buying at 5% ETH Supply Cap

Bitmine now holds 6,085,564 ETH, or 4.98% of the 122.2 million in existence. Its stated goal is 5%, roughly 6.11 million ETH.

That leaves about 24,400 ETH to buy. At last week’s pace of 7,819 ETH, Bitmine would reach its target in about three weeks.

What happens after that matters for Bitmine stock. The weekly purchases have steadily driven demand for ETH, and Bitmine has said it would stop buying at 5%. With the stock below the value of its holdings, buybacks may use new money better than buying more ETH.

Most of the coins are already working. Bitmine stakes about 5.23 million ETH, 86% of its holdings, which it says earns about $245 million a year at current prices.

ETH trades at $1,698, below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $2,113, and its 200-day EMA at $2,242.

Lee has made a fair case that ETH is as scarce as Bitcoin. For Bitmine stock, though, the share count matters as much as the coin count, and that has grown far faster.

Ripple's U.S. dollar stablecoin Ripple USD (RLUSD) has overtaken Gram (GRAM), the token previously known as Toncoin, in the CoinMarketCap ranking of cryptocurrencies by market capitalization.

According to CoinMarketCap data, RLUSD had a market capitalization of $2.82 billion on Tuesday and ranked No. 26, and Gram dropped to No. 27 with a market capitalization of $2.79 billion.

Gram fell below $1 and was trading at around $0.97 on Tuesday, down about 6% over the past seven days, according to CoinMarketCap. The 24-hour trading volume of Gram stood at around $47 million, and RLUSD had about $368 million in trading volume over the same period.

World Liberty Financial USD (USD1) also had a market capitalization of $2.82 billion on Tuesday and was one spot higher, at No. 25. Among stablecoins, Tether (USDT) and USDC still lead the list with $174.64 billion and $69.22 billion, respectively.

According to the terms, the wallet is operated by RAZOR UNIVERSAL CORP., a Panamanian company, and Telegram provides the apps through which users access it. "Telegram does not operate Gram Wallet, does not hold your keys or assets, and is not a party to these Terms," the document says.

The terms also say that "neither we nor Telegram can freeze, seize, move, recover or reverse your assets." At the same time, according to the terms, "anyone who visits your Telegram profile may be able to see your associated Gram Wallet address," as well as the total balance of the wallet. The two coins are now separated by about $30 million, and they are heading in opposite directions. RLUSD has more than doubled in a year. USD1 has lost almost half its supply since February.

Meanwhile, XRP, the token closely tied to Ripple, trades near $0.93, down 26% this month.

So how did Ripple’s dollar catch up, and does it help XRP?

We pulled the daily supply of both coins from DefiLlama’s stablecoin dashboard, which adds up every chain they run on.

We also checked the contracts directly. RLUSD has $2.04 billion on Ethereum and $761 million on the XRP Ledger. USD1 is spread across BNB Chain ($1.10 billion), Solana ($868 million) and Ethereum ($852 million).

RLUSD’s growth has come in steps. Supply jumped from about $1.5 billion to $2.4 billion in August, then climbed again from late October.

The XRP Ledger matters most for XRP holders. About $761 million of RLUSD sits there, roughly a quarter of the total. That is where RLUSD activity can create demand for XRP, which pays the ledger’s fees.

XRP trades at $0.9295, below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $1.1499, and its 200-day EMA at $1.2996.

The next Ripple news test is whether RLUSD can retake the lead and hold it. For XRP, the signal to watch is simpler: a daily close back above $1.00 while sellers keep fading.

#5095. Binance Hack: US Moves to Recover $1.1 Billion, but Who Gets the Money?

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Nearly four weeks after the Binance hack, US authorities have filed a civil forfeiture complaint seeking more than $1.1 billion in USDC linked to the October theft. The money is already subject to restrictions, but the latest court filings reveal a complication: freezing stolen cryptocurrency is considerably easier than returning it.

The complaint, filed on November 23, in the US District Court for the District of Columbia, targets USDC associated with 36 cryptocurrency addresses across 18 blockchains.

Federal investigators attribute the October 29 attack to North Korean hacking groups, including the Lazarus Group. The complaint puts the value of the original theft at approximately $6 billion.

For Binance, the latest legal action represents another opportunity to recover a portion of its losses. For the wider cryptocurrency industry, however, the case raises questions about the authority stablecoin issuers exercise over digital assets and what happens when governments become involved.

The assets targeted by US authorities are not an entirely new discovery.

Earlier this month, NewsBTC reported that Circle had frozen approximately $1.1 billion in USDC linked to the Binance hack, following cooperation with law enforcement.

What has changed is the government’s attempt to establish a legal basis for taking possession of those assets.

According to the court documents, US authorities obtained a temporary restraining order on November 12. Prosecutors subsequently requested that the restrictions remain in place throughout the civil forfeiture proceedings.

Both Binance and Circle consented to the initial restraining order and the requested extension, according to the government’s November 23 application.

The agreement between the companies and federal authorities reduces one immediate obstacle to preserving the funds. It does not, however, resolve the question of their ultimate ownership or distribution.

Civil forfeiture proceedings are directed against property believed to be connected to criminal activity. Interested parties can assert legitimate claims to that property through the legal process.

In this case, prosecutors are seeking forfeiture of the assets to the United States. That is not the same thing as a court ordering their immediate return to Binance.

Perhaps the most interesting disclosure in the complaint concerns Circle itself.

The stablecoin issuer can restrict transfers involving USDC held at particular blockchain addresses. However, that authority does not necessarily give Circle direct control over the wallets holding those tokens.

does not have the technical ability to transfer the Defendant Property from the blocklisted Subject Addresses to the United States

Instead, Circle has agreed to issue an equivalent amount of replacement USDC and transfer those tokens to US authorities upon receiving a forfeiture order from the court.

The proposed arrangement exposes an unusual feature of centralized stablecoins. An issuer can prevent tokens from circulating without possessing the private keys needed to move them.

It also raises an accounting question that deserves attention. If replacement tokens are issued, what ultimately happens to the original frozen USDC, and how will Circle ensure that the treatment of those balances is reflected accurately in its outstanding supply and reserve reporting?

The issuance of replacement tokens would not, by itself, prove that USDC had become undercollateralized. Nevertheless, transparency around the implementation would be important for a stablecoin whose credibility depends on confidence in its backing.

The immediate concern is not whether Circle can create new tokens. It is whether the entire recovery process can be independently accounted for.

The temptation to describe the Justice Department’s announcement as a billion-dollar recovery is understandable. It is also premature.

There are three separate stages involved: restricting access to the stolen assets, obtaining legal authority over them and determining how they will ultimately be distributed.

The November 23 filings advance the second stage. They do not establish that the third has been completed.

There is also a cross-border complication.

On November 18, Reuters reported that an Abu Dhabi court had directed several cryptocurrency companies, including Circle, to preserve digital assets associated with the Binance theft.

The involvement of authorities in both the United States and the United Arab Emirates illustrates how a single cryptocurrency theft can generate legal proceedings across multiple jurisdictions.

Blockchain transactions may cross national borders without much difficulty. Establishing ownership rights over the assets involved is a considerably less straightforward exercise.

That does not mean the US and UAE proceedings are necessarily in conflict. But the ultimate disposition of the funds will require more than an announcement from either government.

For investors assessing Binance’s financial position, the distinction between frozen assets and recovered capital is particularly important. Restricted cryptocurrency should not automatically be treated as money already returned to the exchange.

For years, the ability of stablecoin issuers to freeze tokens has been criticized by advocates of decentralized finance.

The Binance case demonstrates the other side of that argument.

Without Circle’s ability to restrict transactions, preserving such a large amount of cryptocurrency for potential recovery would have been more difficult.

In this particular case, centralized control has provided a mechanism that may help prevent suspected criminals from benefiting from stolen assets.

The uncomfortable question is whether the cryptocurrency industry can benefit from that authority while also demanding meaningful safeguards against its misuse.

The answer depends partly on transparency. Token holders should be able to understand why assets were frozen, under what legal authority restrictions remain in place and how disputes over ownership are resolved.

The same standard should apply to the exchange, the stablecoin issuer and the government.

The next significant development in the Binance case will be the court’s treatment of the forfeiture claim and any competing claims to the assets. Circle’s proposed issuance of replacement USDC will also deserve scrutiny if it proceeds.

Until then, the $1.1 billion should be understood as assets subject to an ongoing recovery effort, not a completed repayment.

For a cryptocurrency industry that frequently celebrates the speed of moving money, the Binance hack is a reminder that getting it back can be an entirely different business.

#5094. JPMorgan, HSBC and StoneX Trade Digital Gold in London as Tokenized Gold Holdings Jump 48%

London is testing tokenized gold as Tether Gold and PAX Gold holdings climb 48% to $4.6 billion despite falling gold prices.

JPMorgan, HSBC and StoneX completed the first live wholesale trades of fractional tokenized gold in London last week. The test is meant to keep the world’s largest gold market ahead of Asian rivals. The three firms also used the digital gold as collateral, without moving a single bar out of the vaults.

Bloomberg reported the trades on Tuesday. They ran on a system built by the World Gold Council (WGC), the industry body that led the project. David Tait, the WGC’s chief executive, called it “a historic step forward for the gold market.”

JPMORGAN $JPM, HSBC AND STONEX COMPLETE THE FIRST LIVE WHOLESALE TRADES OF FRACTIONAL DIGITAL GOLD IN LONDON, ALSO USING IT AS COLLATERAL pic.twitter.com/bwVAdrpkXh

— The Wolf Of All Streets (@scottmelker) November 24, 2026

The banks did not say how much gold changed hands. The system is still in testing, and there is no date yet for a wider launch. The timing is awkward for gold itself. The metal trades near $3,626 an ounce, 32% below its January record and 11% lower than a year ago.

What changes for London’s bullion market, and does it matter for crypto’s own gold tokens?

The WGC calls the new format “pooled gold interests.” Each one is a fractional, electronically transferable share in a pool of physical bars held in approved London vaults.

That fills a gap. Most London trades today are in unallocated gold, which is cheap to hold but leaves buyers as creditors if their bank fails. Allocated gold means owning specific bars, which is safer but costly and hard to split. The WGC proposed the pooled model with law firm Linklaters in September 2025 as a third route between the two.

The collateral piece matters most. Banks could pledge gold for loans and margin as easily as they post bonds, without trucks or vault transfers.

London has a lot riding on it. Its over-the-counter market handles more than $180 billion of gold trades a day, and its vaults held $1.4 trillion of gold in August. Hong Kong, working with the Shanghai Gold Exchange, began testing its own gold clearing system in July.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best Low-Cap Crypto

The London pilot is a closed, bank-only system. Crypto has run its own version for years with Tether Gold (XAUT) and PAX Gold (PAXG), and those tokens have been growing fast.

We read the supply of both tokens straight from their Ethereum contracts, where each token equals one troy ounce. We compared that with CoinGecko’s figures from a year ago.

So crypto’s digital gold kept adding ounces even as the gold price fell. Still, the two tokens hold about 0.33% of the value of gold sitting in London’s vaults. The whole tokenized gold category traded about $329 million in the past 24 hours on CoinGecko, against London’s $180 billion a day.

PAX Gold tracks the metal closely. On Binance, PAXG trades at $3,637, below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $3,945, and its 200-day EMA at $4,195.

Last week’s sell-off pushed it to $3,491 on Saturday, its lowest level in 300 days. Sellers led on Binance’s spot market, where the token itself changes hands. Orders that sold at the market price right away outweighed buyers by a net $13.4 million over the past seven days.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Reveals Upcoming Coinbase Listings

The WGC still has to settle governance rules and a launch date. If the big banks adopt digital gold for collateral, the gap between London’s vaults and crypto’s gold tokens could start to close.

#5092. Saylor Spots New Role for Bitcoin

Strategy Executive Chairman Michael Saylor sees new ways to put Bitcoin (BTC) to work on Wall Street.

According to staff at the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), Bitcoin can be used to meet certain financial resource requirements for U.S. derivatives exchanges and clearinghouses.

‘Next step for adoption is using Bitcoin to work,’ Saylor wrote on X in response to the CFTC advisory published on Nov. 23.

As per the guidance, these companies must maintain sufficient financial resources to cover their operating costs for at least a year.

As clarified by CFTC staff, Bitcoin and Ether can be used to meet this requirement (as well as payment stablecoins). The advisory also provides guidance on how staff interpret the current rules. It also applies to swap execution facilities (SEFs), which are platforms where counterparties trade swaps.

Bitcoin holdings worth $10 million could count for $8 million toward the annual requirement, based on the minimum 20% discount that CFTC staff said they would accept. This provides some flexibility in case Bitcoin's price falls. The discount is also called a haircut.

For Ether, the same minimum 20% haircut applies. For payment stablecoins, the haircut is 2%.

This provides some incentive for an exchange to actually hold BTC. Exchanges could hold Bitcoin on their balance sheets and use some of its value to satisfy this reserve requirement. There would be no need to sell it for USD first.

However, a futures exchange still needs to have sufficient unencumbered cash or highly liquid securities to cover its operating costs for at least six months. Bitcoin, Ether and even payment stablecoins do not fall into this category.

The same six-month liquidity requirement applies to clearinghouses. Additionally, they need to maintain sufficient financial resources to cover a default by a clearing member.

CFTC staff also noted a potential downside for exchanges holding crypto reserves. During a market slump, there's a risk that an exchange's operating losses might rise. At the same time, the value of the Bitcoin it holds to cover those losses might fall.

So this possibility should be considered before an exchange decides whether to use Bitcoin to meet its financial resource requirements.

Each account trading on the XRP Ledger's decentralized exchange moved an average of 4,328 XRP a day in the third quarter of 2026, up 437% from 805 XRP in the same quarter a year earlier, according to a report that XRP treasury company Evernorth released on Tuesday.

According to Evernorth, the average swap on the XRP Ledger reached 35 XRP in the third quarter, up from 19 XRP in the second quarter and under 6 XRP a year earlier. "The growth came from bigger trades, not more of them," the company wrote in the report.

At the same time, the number of accounts trading on the XRP Ledger's order book fell to 1,042 a day in the third quarter of 2026 from 2,027 a day in the third quarter of 2025. The number stood at 1,203 in the fourth quarter of 2025, 1,324 in the first quarter of 2026 and 1,125 in the second quarter, according to the report.

Order-book volume on the XRP Ledger rose to 4.51 million XRP a day in the third quarter from 1.63 million XRP a day a year earlier, Evernorth data shows.

In total, 5.16 million XRP a day was traded on the XRP Ledger's exchange in the third quarter, and the figure was up 96% year over year, according to Evernorth.

Measured in U.S. dollars, exchange volume on the XRP Ledger fell 15% year over year in the third quarter of 2026, according to the report.

Evernorth also compared the XRP Ledger with Ethereum, BNB Chain, Solana, Base, Arbitrum, Avalanche and Polygon. Across these seven networks, exchange volume in dollars fell 42% over the same period, the report shows.

XRP was trading at around $0.93 on Tuesday morning after reaching as high as $1.026 on Monday, according to CoinMarketCap.

The report also shows that the average balance of Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin on the XRP Ledger reached $937 million in the third quarter of 2026, up from $539 million in the second quarter. By the end of the quarter, the RLUSD balance on the XRP Ledger stood at $1.15 billion, compared with $670 million at the end of the second quarter, and the number of RLUSD holders on the network rose to 67,449 from 45,620.

According to Evernorth, the XRP Ledger's average share of RLUSD reached 48.5% in the third quarter, up from 34% in the second quarter. Still, Ethereum finished the quarter with more RLUSD than the XRP Ledger. Evernorth noted that on Ethereum, RLUSD "can already be lent," and that on the XRP Ledger, "native lending is in validator voting."

As of Nov. 20, the Lending Protocol amendment had 24 of 35 validator votes, according to XRPScan. The amendment needs 29 votes, held for 14 days, to activate.

Evernorth completed its business combination with Armada Acquisition Corp. II on Oct. 9, and its shares began trading on Nasdaq under the ticker XRPN on Oct. 12. The company entered the public markets holding approximately 473 million XRP, according to its press release.

Evernorth announced the deal in October 2025, with investments from SBI, Ripple, Pantera Capital, Kraken and GSR.

#5089. Does South Korea’s draft bill give banks control of won-backed stablecoins?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

The South Korean FSC’s new draft bill could change things for the country’s crypto space. What’s what’s going on exactly?

Under the new plan, banks put together can own more than half of any won stablecoin issuer. A fintech company can still be the largest shareholder, but they can’t run the show alone anymore.

Issuers must have FSC approval and at least 5 billion won in equity. Reserves must cover 100% of tokens in circulation, and holders must be able to cash out at face value right away.

As far as exchanges go, one shareholder can hold 20% or 34% with FSC approval. They’ll also need separate licences for dealing, brokerage, and custody.

South Korea’s plan is a 22% tax on crypto gains above 2.5 million won a year. It was meant to kick in this January, but it looks like that date’s been pushed back to 2029.

One reason is that it’s the earliest Korea can start swapping crypto tax data with the United States.

If that happens, it won’t be the first delay. The tax was first proposed back in 2020 and has been shelved several times since.

Enforcement is still active though. AMBCrypto previously reported that 27 unlicensed exchange websites were blocked recently, including KuCoin, MEXC and BingX. This was after their apps were already restricted.

Users on those platforms are being nudged towards the country’s 28 licensed exchanges.

#5088. Bitcoin Loses $60,000 And Gold Offers No Protection During Its Worst Selloff Since 1982

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

The Bitcoin price fell back below $60,000 on Tuesday, cutting short a recovery that had taken the cryptocurrency above $64,000 a day earlier. But perhaps the more troubling development for investors is happening outside the crypto market.

Gold is going through a severe correction of its own, leaving investors in two assets often associated with wealth preservation facing substantial losses.

This is not the first time Bitcoin and gold have struggled simultaneously. What makes the current environment particularly difficult is that neither asset generates income at a time when interest-bearing investments offer an increasingly attractive alternative.

The question is no longer simply whether Bitcoin is digital gold. It is whether investors have enough reason to own either asset under current monetary conditions.

The selling extended well beyond Bitcoin. Figures from the World Gold Council show that Bitcoin lost 13.7%, gold fell 8.3% and the Nasdaq dropped 10%, while the US Dollar Index gained 0.4%. The numbers point to a broader reduction in risk exposure rather than a selloff specific to crypto.

Gold declined 24.6% over the 60 days ending November 23, its steepest loss over such a period since 1982.

The World Gold Council’s latest market assessment, published on Monday, identified several risks facing the precious metal, including pressure on leveraged equity and credit positions, restrictive monetary policy and the possibility of another disappointing US inflation report.

The organization also identified the lack of a clear reduction in speculative positioning as a concern.

This matters for Bitcoin because the argument for buying BTC during a gold correction often assumes that capital leaving one scarce asset will eventually find its way into the other.

There is little reason to assume that happens automatically.

An investor selling gold to reduce leverage or meet a margin requirement is unlikely to replace that exposure immediately with Bitcoin. The priority is raising cash, not finding another store of value.

There is also a difference between selling an asset because its investment thesis has deteriorated and selling because the cost of maintaining a position has become too expensive. The latter can create opportunities for patient buyers, but it rarely provides a reliable indication of when a market will bottom.

Monday’s trading session offered Bitcoin investors some encouragement. The cryptocurrency recovered above $64,000 following the previous week’s decline to its lowest levels in roughly two years.

The broader picture is hardly encouraging. Bitcoin has lost nearly 24% over the past three months, falling from a period high of $86,578 to a low of $58,178. Although BTC has since recovered above $60,000, the bounce has done little to change the broader downward trend.

Tuesday’s return below $60,000 raises questions about the strength of the recovery, particularly given the improvement in technology stocks during Monday’s session.

If Bitcoin struggles to sustain gains when conditions improve elsewhere, investors should be careful about assuming that another equity market rally will necessarily pull BTC higher.

There is also an important distinction between a recovery driven by fresh buyers and one driven by traders closing profitable short positions. Both can produce impressive green candles. Only the former demonstrates that investors are willing to commit new capital at higher prices.

Spot trading activity, ETF subscriptions and derivatives positioning will offer a better indication of which type of recovery the market is experiencing.

For now, the failure to retain Monday’s gains makes the rebound less convincing than its initial size suggested.

Bitcoin’s recent performance will inevitably revive criticism of its role as a store of value. However, gold’s own losses make that argument considerably less straightforward.

The metal has been used to preserve wealth for centuries, yet it remains vulnerable to changes in interest rates, investor positioning and the strength of the US dollar.

Bitcoin shares some of those vulnerabilities while carrying considerably different market risks, including its dependence on speculative demand and the availability of leverage across cryptocurrency exchanges.

That does not invalidate Bitcoin’s scarcity argument. Its supply characteristics have not changed because its market price has fallen.

What the current correction does challenge is the assumption that scarcity alone guarantees protection during financial stress.

An asset can have a credible long-term investment case and still be a poor short-term hedge. Bitcoin investors would benefit from separating those two propositions rather than defending both every time the market declines.

The immediate focus now turns to Wednesday’s US inflation release.

The Bureau of Economic Analysis is scheduled to publish its October personal consumption expenditures (PCE) report on November 25. The previous release showed annual headline PCE inflation of 3.6%, with core inflation at 3.1%.

Another stronger-than-expected reading could reinforce expectations of restrictive monetary policy, making conditions more difficult for assets that rely heavily on capital appreciation.

A softer reading, particularly if accompanied by falling Treasury yields, could offer some relief to both Bitcoin and gold.

For Bitcoin, however, recovering $60,000 should be treated as a starting point rather than confirmation of a broader reversal. Monday’s trading high above $64,000 represents a more demanding test of whether buyers are prepared to return.

Until that happens, the market has demonstrated that it can bounce. It has yet to demonstrate that it can sustain a recovery.
